content.text: I've inspected every audit/inspection/verification location. No Vendor audit right against Customer exists.

input.quote: C. Audits. M&I shall cause a third party review of its data processing center, the Operations Center, and related internal controls to be conducted annually by its independent auditors. M&I shall provide without charge to Customer, upon written request, one copy of the audit report resulting from such review.
input.rationale: Every audit, examination and verification right in the Agreement runs in our favour or to our regulators, not against us: § 21.9(C) (p0277) obliges M&I to procure an annual independent third-party review of its own data centre and internal controls and to give us the report free of charge; § 21.9(B) (p0276) and § 21.8 (p0274) preserve examination access for our Federal Regulators over M&I's performance and records; § 17.1 (p0243) confirms Customer Data remains subject to examination by our auditors and regulators as if held on our premises; and § 22.12 (p0300) requires M&I to furnish its parent's annual report. Searches for audit/inspect/verify/examine, monitoring, licence-compliance, usage or fee verification, books-and-records access, and remote or on-site access to Customer facilities returned no M&I right to audit Customer's usage, fees or systems. With no Vendor audit right binding us, there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to constrain, so the position sits at or above the preferred checklist and nothing should be redlined (adding an audit-limitation clause would only invite an audit right that does not exist). Noted only, not flagged: § 21.7(C) (p0273) requires us to provide evidence on request that the Agreement is properly reflected on our books — a narrow documentary confirmation of a representation, with no inspection, verification or system-access right, so it is outside this rule's scope.
